Messages.Author: James R. McClure Jr.
Messages.Body:
Angelic Ebbers <ebb...@aries.phys.yorku.ca> wrote:
> By the way, can you use a sudden
> reversal to cancel a sudden reversal?

Peace Angelic,

No, you may not play an SR (which is an Out of Turn Master) during your
own turn.

Nil carborundum illigitimi,

James R. McClure Jr.
The OS/2 Apostle

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
In article <3od8hj$b...@hermes.louisville.edu>,

James R. McClure Jr. <jrmc...@ulkyvm.louisville.edu> wrote:
>Angelic Ebbers <ebb...@aries.phys.yorku.ca> wrote:
>> By the way, can you use a sudden
>> reversal to cancel a sudden reversal?
>
>Peace Angelic,
>
>No, you may not play an SR (which is an Out of Turn Master) during your
>own turn.

To be clear:
The answer to Angelic's question is yes, however,
as it is perfectly legal to SR someone else's SR.
You simply cannot do it on your own turn.

(If you wanted to SR your Prey's SR of a Vulnerability played
by your Prey's Prey, for example).
